sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 5.2(ii), p.956, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 194 (2021), 943–966 (Caltech repository copy of the publisher PDF, SHA-256 77ff3290…790e)
sourceIssues.printed: "(ii) The number of supersingular points in X₀(N)(F_{p²}) that correspond to supersingular elliptic curves over F_{p²} with the Frobenius trace a_{p²} = 2p or −2p and the j-invariant different from 0 and 1728 is at least µ(⌊(p−1)/12⌋ − 3/2 + (−3/p) + ½(−1/p)). In particular, there is a supersingular point with a_{p²} = 2p or −2p in X₀(N)(F_{p²}) over X(1)(F_{p²})∖{0,1728} that is unramified for π if p ≡ 1 mod 12 or p ≥ 31."
sourceIssues.correction: The "in particular" follows for p ≡ 1 mod 12 and for p ≥ 31 with p ≠ 47. At p = 47 the displayed lower bound is 0 and gives nothing. The existence of an unramified supersingular point at p = 47 comes instead from Lemma 5.2(iii), since 47 ≡ 2 mod 3.
sourceIssues.reason: The conclusion needs the lower bound to exceed the number of ramification points, which (i) bounds by µ/6. At p = 47: ⌊46/12⌋ = 3, (−3/47) = −1 (47 ≡ 2 mod 3) and (−1/47) = −1 (47 ≡ 3 mod 4), so the bound is µ(3 − 3/2 − 1 − 1/2) = 0 < µ/6. A computation over all primes 31 ≤ p ≤ 400 finds 47 as the only failure, and beyond that the floor term dominates. The main theorem is unaffected: Lemma 5.2(iii) covers p = 47, and Rubin's own verification (Remark 2.3) covers small p. Found by the review REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.0.2 and Proposition 3.3, pp.951–953; proof of Theorem 3.4, p.954, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 194 (2021), 943–966 (Caltech repository copy of the publisher PDF, SHA-256 77ff3290…790e)
sourceIssues.printed: "Let ν ∈ X_l be a Hecke character of order l^m. We define ξ_ν as the image of z_{fl^m} …" and "Proposition 3.3. Let ν ∈ X_l be a character of order l^m", while the same construction uses K(fl^m p^{n+1}), "the conductor fl^m of ϕν" (proof of 3.3(3)) and "let l^m be the conductor" (p.954).
sourceIssues.correction: Read l^m as the conductor of ν throughout §3.0.2–3.0.3 (so that ν factors through K(fl^m) and the elliptic unit z_{fl^m} applies), with the anticyclotomic layer L_m indexed accordingly.
sourceIssues.reason: For l split in K, the l-part of the ring class group of conductor l^n is (Z/l^n)^×, of order (l−1)l^{n−1}, so an anticyclotomic character of exact order l^m (m ≥ 1) has conductor l^{m+1}, not l^m. The construction and the proofs use l^m as the conductor, so "order" is the slip; nothing else changes. The extraction silently used the conductor reading.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.8, p.960, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 194 (2021), 943–966 (Caltech repository copy of the publisher PDF, SHA-256 77ff3290…790e)
sourceIssues.printed: "Consider the Coates–Wiles derivative δ : V^∗_∞/V^{∗,−}_∞ → O."
sourceIssues.correction: Say why δ factors through the quotient: on U^∗_∞ one has δ₁ = (1 − π^{−1})δ = (1 + p^{−1})δ, where δ₁ is the character derivative at the trivial character; the trivial character lies in Ξ⁺, and V^{∗,−}_∞ kills δ_χ for every χ in Ξ⁺, so δ vanishes on V^{∗,−}_∞.
sourceIssues.reason: δ is defined on U^∗_∞, and its vanishing on V^{∗,−}_∞ is used but not stated. It follows from the relation between δ and δ₁ together with the parity convention of §2. Found by the review REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21.
